translation_en: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, told him that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, rode a donkey with a Fadaki cloak over it, and seated Usamah ibn Zayd behind him. He was going to visit Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah among Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, before the Battle of Badr. He said: He passed by a gathering in which were ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul—this was before ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had accepted Islam—and a mixed group of Muslims, idol-worshipping polytheists, Jews, and Muslims. ‘Abd Allah ibn Rawahah was also in the gathering. When the dust raised by the animal reached the gathering, ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak and said, ‘Do not cover us with dust.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, greeted them, then stopped, dismounted, and invited them to Allah and recited the Quran to them. ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said, ‘Man, there is nothing better than what you say, if it is true. But do not bother us with it in our gathering. Go back to your mount, and whoever comes to you, tell it to him.’ ‘Abd Allah ibn Rawahah said, ‘Yes indeed, Messenger of Allah, bring it to us in our gatherings, for we love that.’ The Muslims, polytheists, and Jews began insulting one another, and they nearly came to blows. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, kept calming them until they became quiet. Then the Prophet mounted his animal and continued until he entered upon Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah. The Prophet said to him, ‘Sa‘d, did you hear what Abu Hubab said?’—meaning ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy—‘and what he said?’ Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah replied, ‘Messenger of Allah, pardon him and overlook it. By the One who sent down the Book to you, Allah has brought you the truth that He sent down to you. The people of this lake had agreed to crown him and bind the royal turban around him, but when Allah, by the truth He gave you, prevented that, he was consumed with resentment over it. That is why he behaved as you saw.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, pardoned him. The Prophet and his Companions used to pardon the polytheists and the People of the Book, as Allah had commanded them, and they patiently bore harm. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘You will surely hear much hurtful speech from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah’ (3:186). Allah also said, ‘Many of the People of the Book wish that they could turn you back into disbelievers after your faith, out of envy from within themselves…’ (2:109), through the end of the verse. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, acted upon the pardon that Allah had commanded him, until Allah gave him permission concerning them. When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, fought at Badr and Allah killed the leading Quraysh disbelievers through that battle, ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and those with him among the polytheists and idol-worshippers said, ‘This matter has now become established.’ They pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, to accept Islam, and so they accepted Islam.
